name: composability
title: Composability: a boundary controller process perturbing the biofilm at runtime
question:
Does viva-biofilm's boundary_concentrations runtime hook (the Task 6
set_bulk_by_name binding) actually compose with an external
process-bigraph control process -- can a BoundaryControllerProcess drive
the biofilm's oxygen boundary on a schedule and produce a visible,
measurable growth response, the same way process-bigraph composes any two
processes sharing a store?

report.title: Composability
report.evidence_quality: deterministic paired run (fixed seed for both perturbed and control arms, no statistical repeats)
report.objective:
Couple a new BoundaryControllerProcess to BiofilmProcess via a shared
boundary_concentrations store, drive oxygen down at t=1d and restore it
at t=3d over a 4-day run, and compare against an identically-seeded
un-perturbed control to demonstrate that the biofilm's growth responds
to a runtime, externally-driven environmental perturbation.
report.result:
The controller followed its schedule exactly: oxygen boundary held at
0.5 g/m^3 (reference 0.5) through the t=1d-3d low window and restored to
8.74 g/m^3 (reference 8.74) after. Over the same 4-day, same-seed window,
the perturbed biofilm's growth was visibly suppressed relative to the
control: final population 60 vs. 120 agents, final total biomass 11.58
pg vs. 20.08 pg (biomass ratio 0.577) -- a clear, measurable response to
the runtime boundary perturbation.
report.interpretation:
The Task 6 runtime boundary hook and the Task 7 controller process
compose exactly the way any two process-bigraph processes sharing a
store should: no biofilm-internal code changed, yet an external process
can meaningfully steer the simulation's environment and produce a
biologically sensible response (oxygen limitation slows growth). This
demonstrates viva-biofilm's composability with process-bigraph beyond
the single-process biofilm/chemostat composites.
